newsitem.title: USA: PP&L sees Susquehanna 1 back fully next week.
newsitem.headline: PP&L sees Susquehanna 1 back fully next week.

text.p: Pennsylvania Power & Light Co (PP&L) Thursday said it expected the 1,090 megawatt (MW) Susquehanna 1 nuclear power unit to resume full output early next week following its ninth refueling outage.
"Actual testing is about six days," said an onsite spokesman, referring to the time required for various startup tests between restart and full service.
The Berwick, Pa., unit began contributing electricity to the grid at about 1830 EDT on Wednesday, an onsite spokesman said, adding it was producing power at 20 percent of capacity.
Susquehanna 1's 47-day refueling and maintenance shutdown began Sept 7.
The neighboring 1,094 MW Susquehanna 2 was generating at 100 percent output.
The two Susquehanna units are jointly owned by PP&L and Allegheny Electric Cooperative Inc.
The Susquehanna facility accounts for 30 percent of PP&L power deliveries and 20 percent of its installed generation capacity.
